args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 (latest production deploy) was failing health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of 18%. Rolled back all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, the service reports healthy on v2.3.0 in all regions, with an error rate of 0.2%. Note: v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging before v2.3.1 went to production. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure and review why an RC that failed in staging was promoted.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened the SEV2 incident.

- **Rollback:** The latest deploy, v2.3.1, was failing health checks in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an 18% error rate. v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production, so I rolled back to it. All three regions now run v2.3.0, and the service reports healthy with a 0.2% error rate.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api) is open and the on-call engineer has been paged. It describes the failure, the rollback and the recovery numbers.

One thing to follow up: v2.3.1's release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) was also failing in staging before v2.3.1 went to production. I put this in the incident as a follow-up item, along with finding the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
